en: The client approved this change at {col:changes.price} and {col:changes.days} extra days. The contract value and the budget change by this amount, and the extra days move the planned finish.
Please sign below to confirm that both parties agree the price and the time.
Project: {col:daywork.proj}. Date of the work: {col:daywork.date}. Work done: {col:daywork.desc}.
The work took {col:daywork.hours} labour hours. With materials and plant the value of the sheet is {col:daywork.value}.
Please sign the attached sheet so that we can include it in the next invoice.
We had to put right or pay for work that is your responsibility. The cost is {col:backcharges.amount} plus an administration fee of {col:backcharges.fee}, a total of {col:backcharges.total}.
We will deduct this from your next payment unless you tell us within seven days why it should not apply.

The budget is {col:projects.budget}, the cost to date is {col:projects.actual} and the forecast final cost is {col:projects.eac}. The forecast profit is {col:projects.forecast}, a margin of {col:projects.margin_pct}. The bid margin was {col:projects.bid_margin}.
We ask for a decision on the actions to protect the margin: change orders to claim, savings to take and costs to challenge.
The transfer moves budget from {col:transfers.from_code} to {col:transfers.to_code}. Reason: {col:transfers.reason}.
The approval level for this amount is: {col:transfers.state}. The total budget of the project does not change.
The allowance is {col:provsum.allowance} and we have spent {col:provsum.spent}. What is left is {col:provsum.left}.
If the final cost will be higher than the allowance, we will send the price and ask for your approval before we order.
Value engineering proposal to the client
We expect to save {col:ve.saving} and the change costs {col:ve.cost} to carry out, a net saving of {col:ve.net}. The quality and the use of the building stay the same.
Please tell us if you agree so that we can order and update the budget.
Note on the use of contingency
The contingency was used for: {col:contdraw.desc}. The total drawn on this project is now {col:contdraw.drawn} and what is left is {col:contdraw.left}.
Cover note for a monthly cost report

The value earned was {col:monthly.claimed} against a cost of {col:monthly.cost}, a gross profit of {col:monthly.gross} and a margin of {col:monthly.margin}. The cost to date at the end of the month was {col:monthly.cum}.
Please read the note together with the cost to complete sheet before the monthly review.

Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: markup on changes, overhead, target and lowest margin, warning levels and the labour cost for rework.
List your projects on Project Register with contract value, bid margin and contingency. Budget, cost to date, forecast and margin fill in from the other sheets.
Set the budget of each project on Project Budgets, one row for each cost code. Cost to date, commitments and what is left update by themselves.
Book every invoice and payroll entry on Actual Cost Lines with its project and cost code. Add orders and subcontracts on Committed Costs before the invoice arrives.
Each month update Cost to Complete: the share of work done and the cost still to come for every cost code. The forecast final cost and variance follow.
Record every change on Change Orders with your cost and the days it adds. Send the price, chase the client and see approved changes raise the contract value.
Use Daywork Sheets, Provisional Sums and Backcharges to value extra work, watch allowances and recover money from subcontractors.
Log Rework and Waste, explain overruns on Overruns Explained, move budget on Budget Transfers and record every use of Contingency Drawdown.
Type the value earned on Monthly Cost Report and the forecast margin on Profit Fade, then read Margin Forecast for the outcome of each project.

Use the 14 calculators for variance, estimate at completion, margin, change order price, daywork, earned value, early warning, contingency, backcharges, rework, break-even, price rises, unit cost and profit fade.
Read Job Costing Dashboard and Charts every week: margin at risk, budgets over, overruns without a cause, changes waiting, unsigned daywork and backcharges to recover.
Control materials, suppliers and machines in one workbook
Orders with received and outstanding quantity
each order shows what arrived, what is still due, the open value and a status that turns red when the promised date passes
Three-way match of order, delivery and invoice
every invoice is checked against the price on the order and the quantity you accepted, and shows the amount billed above what you owe
Deliveries with days late and rejected quantity
each delivery note records the quantity delivered and rejected, the days late and the lead time, so suppliers are judged on facts
on-time rate, rejected share and invoice accuracy combine into one score and a rating for every supplier
Requisitions from site with an ordered check
a request is marked ordered only when an order for that project and material exists, and warns when the needed date passes
quantity used is compared with the estimate for each project and material, with the cost of every overrun
Stock on site with reorder level
received minus used gives the stock in the books, the count difference and a reorder warning for every project
service, repair, fuel and hire for each machine are divided by the days it worked, with utilisation and service status
every machine is placed on a project for dates, and the same machine booked twice is flagged
Hire log with a limit for buying
days on hire and cost so far grow each day a machine stays, and a hire past your limit is flagged so you can compare with buying
the average delivery time you really get is compared with the usual lead time and tells you how many days earlier to order

Suppliers and what you buy from them
One row for each supplier with terms; orders, spend, open order value, delivery score and rating fill in from the orders, deliveries and invoices.
Projects that buy materials and use equipment
One row for each project with its manager; orders, value ordered, share of the contract, late orders, open requisitions and equipment cost fill in.
Material catalogue with budget price and what you really pay
One row for each material with its budget price, waste and usual lead time; quantity and value ordered, the average price paid and whether prices are rising fill in.
One row for each request from site with the date it is needed; the project, the manager phone, quantity already ordered and a status that warns when nothing is ordered fill in.
Purchase orders with what arrived and what is still due
One row for each order with supplier, project, quantity, price and promised date; value, quantity received, what is outstanding, invoiced value and a status that flags late orders fill in.
Deliveries and goods received against each order
One row for each delivery note with the quantity delivered and rejected; the supplier, the ordered quantity, days late, lead time and whether it was on time fill in.
Supplier invoices matched to orders and deliveries
One row for each invoice; the order, what was received and the price on the order fill in, then a three-way check, the amount billed above what you owe and the payment status.
One row for each project and material with the quantity estimated and the quantity used; ordered and received quantities, the overrun and its cost, and a status fill in.
Stock on site for each project and material
One row for each project and material with the last count; received, used, the stock the books show, the difference and a status that says when to reorder fill in.
One row for each price you were quoted or paid; the budget price, the change against it and whether the price is rising fill in.
One row for each machine with its day rate and service interval; days used, cost of service, fuel and downtime, cost per day used, utilisation and whether it needs a service fill in.
One row each time a machine goes to a project, with the dates; days, cost at the day rate and a warning when the same machine is booked twice fill in.
Hire log with on-hire and off-hire dates
One row for each hire with the dates and the agreed day rate; days on hire, cost so far and a flag when a hire runs past your limit fill in. Leave the off-hire date empty while it is still on site.
One row for each service, inspection or repair with its cost and next due date; the machine name, days to the next service and a status that warns before a service is due fill in.
Fuel log by machine and project
One row for each refill with litres and the price of one litre; cost and the machine name fill in, and cost for each project adds up.
One row for each breakdown with the days lost and the repair cost; the lost value at the day rate and a flag for long stops fill in.
One row each time tools go to site, with who took them; the value, the days out and a status that flags tools not returned in time fill in.
Supplier performance: on time, quality and invoices
One row for each supplier with complaints you logged; deliveries, on-time rate, rejected share, invoices that matched, a score out of 100 and a rating fill in from the other sheets.
Lead times: what the supplier says and what you get
One row for each material with the safety days you add; the usual lead time, the real average from deliveries, the gap and when to order earlier fill in.
Order this many days before use
Returns and credit notes from suppliers
One row for each return with the quantity and the credit received so far; the supplier, the value returned, the credit still due and whether you should chase it fill in.

Type the area, the coats and the coverage of the paint, and the size of the tile; see the litres of paint, the number of tiles with waste and both costs.
Type how many days a year you need it, the hire rate, the price to buy, its resale value, the years you keep it and the yearly upkeep; see the cheaper choice and the days where buying starts to win.

Tell a supplier a new order is coming
Hello {contact}, we will send you a new purchase order this week. Please keep the stock and tell us the earliest delivery date.
Ask a supplier for a quote
Hello {contact}, can you send a price and the delivery time for the next order? Please include the delivery charge and your payment terms.
Hello {contact}, we confirm payment terms of {terms} days from the date of the invoice. Please write them on every invoice.
Hello {contact}, your delivery score with us is {score} out of 100 and your rating is {rating}. We would like to talk about how to improve it.
Hello, our order {po_id}: {qty} {unit} of {item} for {pname}, needed on {promised}. Please confirm the date.
Hello, please confirm that you received our order {po_id} for {item} and that you can deliver on {promised}.
Hello, order {po_id} for {item} was promised for {promised} and is {days_over} days late. Please tell us the delivery day today.
Ask for the rest of an order
Hello, we received only part of order {po_id}. We still wait for {outstanding} {unit} of {item}. When will the rest arrive?
Ask to bring a delivery forward
Hello, can you deliver order {po_id} ({item}) before {promised}? Site is ready and we can receive it any day.
Hello, we must cancel the open part of order {po_id} for {item}. Please confirm that nothing else will be sent.
Hello, delivery {del_id} for order {po}: {rej} of {item} arrived damaged and we rejected them. Please send a replacement and collect the damaged goods.
Hello, delivery {del_id} for order {po} was short. We counted {qty} of {ordered} ordered. Please send the rest.
Thank a supplier for a good delivery
Hello, thank you for delivery {del_id} of {item}. It arrived complete and on time and the site is happy.
Hello, invoice {inv_id} charges {price} for {item}, but the order price was {po_price}. Please send a corrected invoice.
Hello, invoice {inv_id} bills {qty} of {item}, but we accepted {received}. Please send a corrected invoice.
Hello, invoice {inv_id} for {billed} is due on {due}. We will pay it on that day.
Tell a supplier an invoice is paid
Hello, we paid invoice {inv_id} for {billed}. Please check your account and send us a receipt.
Ask a supplier to collect a return
Hello, please collect {qty} of {item} from order {po}. The reason for the return is on our return note {r_id}.
Hello, we returned goods on {date} under {r_id}. The credit we wait for is {due}. Please send the credit note.
Hello, the credit for return {r_id} is {days} days old and still not received ({due}). Please send it this week or we will hold the next payment.
Ask a hire company to collect
Hello, we finished with the {item} on {pname}. Please collect it and stop the hire from today.
Hello, we need the {item} for more time on {pname}. Please keep the rate of {rate} a day and confirm the new end date.
Ask for a better rate on a long hire
Hello, the {item} has been with us for {days} days. Can you give a lower daily rate than {rate} for the rest of the hire?
Warn a manager about late orders
Hello, {name} has {late} late orders. Please check the delivery plan with the supervisor today.
Remind a manager about open requests
Hello, {name} has {openreq} requisitions waiting for an order. Please approve them so that the buyer can order.
Hello, materials ordered for {name} so far are {ordered}, which is {share} of the contract value. Please review the usage against the estimate.
Tell a manager an order is placed
Hello, your request {rq_id} for {item} on {pname} has been ordered. We will tell you the delivery day.
Hello, we need the quantity and the day needed for request {rq_id} ({item}) on {pname}. Please reply today so that we can order.
Purchase order letter to a supplier
Please supply {col:po.qty} {col:po.unit} of {col:po.item} at {col:po.price} for each unit. The order value is {col:po.value}.
Delivery is needed by {col:po.promised}. Please confirm the date and send the delivery note with the goods, showing this order number.
We will check the quantity and condition on arrival and pay against the invoice on your agreed terms.
The order for {col:po.item} was promised for {col:po.promised}. We still wait for {col:po.outstanding} {col:po.unit}, which is {col:po.days_over} days late.
The delay stops work on site. Please confirm in writing the day you will deliver. If you cannot, tell us today so that we can order from another supplier.
The invoice is for {col:inv.qty} units at {col:inv.price}, a total of {col:inv.billed}. Our order was for a price of {col:inv.po_price} and we have received and accepted {col:inv.received} units.
The amount billed above the order is {col:inv.over}. Please send a corrected invoice or a credit note. We will pay the correct amount on its due date.
We returned {col:returns.qty} of {col:returns.item} on {col:returns.date}. The value is {col:returns.value} and the credit we still wait for is {col:returns.due}.
Please issue the credit note within seven days and tell us the number so that we can match it to your next invoice.
On {col:del.date} we received {col:del.qty} of {col:del.item}. We rejected {col:del.rej} because of its condition or quantity. Condition recorded: {col:del.cond}.
Please collect the rejected goods and send the replacement by the next working day. We will not pay for goods that we have rejected.
